metadata.purpose: Calibration data for Epoch sprint_forecast tool
metadata.scope: Publicly available, anonymized agile estimation and velocity data from industry reports, academic research, and published benchmarks
metadata.caution: Story points are team-relative and not standardized across teams. All point-based figures should be used as distributional priors, not absolute targets. Combine with team-specific historical data for best results.

storyPointsPerSprintPerDeveloper.description: Story points completed per 2-week sprint per developer (team-relative, not comparable across teams)
storyPointsPerSprintPerDeveloper.notes: New Scrum teams typically average 5-10 SP/person/sprint (Atlassian). PM Toolkit reports 8-12 SP/person/sprint as typical. Individual productivity varies with task complexity, role mix, and team dynamics.

teamVelocityBySize.description: Typical team velocity per 2-week sprint by team size

velocityStabilityCoefficient.description: Coefficient of variation (CV = std_dev / mean) for sprint-to-sprint velocity

excellent_threshold.description: Excellent consistency; team can reliably commit to velocity range. Associated with 85-95% commitment accuracy.

concerning_threshold.description: High volatility; sprint planning becomes unreliable

highVolatility_threshold.description: Indicates inconsistent estimation, changing requirements, team changes, tech debt, or external dependencies

typical_healthy_range.description: Healthy teams with stable velocity and mature processes
typical_healthy_range.source: Aggregated from Toolsbase Agile Metrics Calculator (https://toolsbase.dev/en/agile/agile-metrics-calculator) and GrowingScrumMasters (https://www.growingscrummasters.com/keywords/velocity-stability/)

healthy_fluctuation.description: +/-15% fluctuation sprint-to-sprint is healthy and expected

warning_drop.description: Velocity drops by 30%+ for 2+ consecutive sprints warrants investigation

sprintCompletionRate.description: Percentage of committed stories/story points actually completed within the sprint

industryAverage_commitDoneRatio.source: Scrum.org benchmarks via CodePulse sprint spillover analysis (https://codepulsehq.com/guides/sprint-spillover-analysis-guide)

sprints_with_spillover.description: Approximately 70% of sprints do not complete all committed work
sprints_with_spillover.source: CodePulse (https://codepulsehq.com/guides/sprint-spillover-analysis-guide), citing State of Agile Reports 2021-2024

teams_regularly_hitting_90plus.description: Less than 20% of teams regularly hit 90%+ sprint completion

highPerforming_target.description: High-performing teams achieve 80%+ sprint commitment completion. Target 85-90% is healthy.
highPerforming_target.source: ContinuousQuest (https://continuousquest.com/agile-metrics-how-can-they-improve-your-team/); Count.co sprint commitment accuracy benchmarks (https://count.co/metric/sprint-commitment-accuracy)

poorPerformance_threshold.description: Below 60% commit done ratio indicates poor sprint plan execution

academic_SPI_median.description: Median Schedule Performance Indicator (completed/committed) across studied sprints
academic_SPI_median.source: UPM academic paper on sprint velocity fluctuations (https://oa.upm.es/id/eprint/38304/contents)

sprint_rollover_patterns.source: Easy Agile State of Team Alignment 2026 (https://easyagile.com/downloads/state-of-team-alignment-report-2026), n=419 engineers/PMs

storyPointToHoursRatio.description: Relationship between story points and actual hours. NOT a fixed conversion -- varies by team and should be used as a distribution.
storyPointToHoursRatio.typicalRange: 1 SP = 3-6 hours of actual development effort
storyPointToHoursRatio.percentWithin1SD: 68% of the time: 1 SP = 3.25 to 4.75 hours
storyPointToHoursRatio.percentWithin2SD: 95% of the time: 1 SP = 2.5 to 5.5 hours
storyPointToHoursRatio.importantCaveat: The relationship between points and hours is not an equivalence. It is a mean with significant variance. Teams are not perfectly consistent in relative estimation, especially for larger stories (8+ points).

sprintLengthDistribution.description: Distribution of sprint/iteration lengths used by Scrum teams
sprintLengthDistribution.source: Parabol 300+ Agile Statistics (https://www.parabol.co/resources/agile-statistics/), aggregated from State of Agile reports

expertEstimationAccuracy.description: Expert-based effort estimation accuracy for software development
expertEstimationAccuracy.directionOfBias: Slight tendency toward underestimation, but not as strong as commonly assumed
expertEstimationAccuracy.source: Jorgensen, M. (2004) 'A Review of Studies on Expert Estimation of Software Development Effort', Journal of Systems and Software, 70(1), pp. 37-60. Via Simula Research Laboratory (https://web-backend.simula.no/sites/default/files/publications/SE.4.Joergensen.2004.c.pdf)
expertEstimationAccuracy.additionalSource: Mike Cohn / Mountain Goat Software summarizes Jorgensen: 'most estimates to be within 20 to 30% of actuals' (https://mountaingoatsoftware.com/blog/are-we-really-bad-at-estimating)

storyPointAccuracy.description: How accurately story point estimates reflect actual effort

featureTasks.description: Mean Magnitude of Relative Error for feature development tasks

bugFixingTasks.description: MRE for bug-fixing tasks -- not significantly different from features

taskLevelMRE.source: Cao, L. 'Estimating Efforts for Various Activities in Agile Software Development: An Empirical Study', IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering. Old Dominion University. n=~7000 task-level estimates across 46 iterations. (https://digitalcommons.odu.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1077&context=itds_facpubs)

estimationDoesNotImproveOverTime.finding: Estimation accuracy does NOT improve over time in agile projects, contrary to agile community belief
estimationDoesNotImproveOverTime.evidence: Kruskal-Wallis test across early/middle/late project phases showed no significant improvement (p=0.0599, H=5.63)

relativeEstimationAlignment.description: How well team story point scales align (e.g., is an 8-point story really 8x a 1-point story)
relativeEstimationAlignment.finding: Teams are 'amazingly consistent' up to 5-point stories. Drift becomes measurable at 8+ points. Example: at one company, 1-point median = 21 hours, 3-point median = 64 hours (near perfect 3x), but 8-point median = 111 hours vs expected 147 (25% drift).
relativeEstimationAlignment.source: Mike Cohn, Mountain Goat Software, with data from one company (https://mountaingoatsoftware.com/blog/seeing-how-well-a-teams-story-points-align-from-one-to-eight)

velocityPredictionAccuracy.description: Velocity prediction accuracy (story points) across multiple studies
velocityPredictionAccuracy.source: CodePulse sprint spillover analysis citing multiple State of Agile Reports (https://codepulsehq.com/guides/sprint-spillover-analysis-guide)

underestimationBias.description: Systematic bias in software effort estimation
underestimationBias.averageEffortOverrun: 100% (i.e., actual effort averages 2x the estimate for underestimated projects)
underestimationBias.source: ISBSG 'Estimates - How Accurate Are They?' (https://isbsg.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/Estimates_-_How_accurate_Are_They_2012.pdf), n=200 projects
underestimationBias.additionalFinding: Jorgensen (2004) found mean effort overrun of 30-40% across surveyed software projects. Feature tasks are underestimated more frequently than bug-fixing/refactoring tasks.

featureVsBug_overestimation.finding: Bug-fixing and refactoring tasks are overestimated more frequently than feature tasks. Feature tasks are underestimated more frequently.

selfReportedAccuracy_vs_Reality.finding: 63% of teams report feeling confident in their estimates, but 44% miss the mark on half their work or more
selfReportedAccuracy_vs_Reality.source: Easy Agile State of Team Alignment 2026 (https://easyagile.com/downloads/state-of-team-alignment-report-2026), n=419

planningPokerAccuracy.description: Accuracy of Planning Poker estimation method

feedbackImprovement.description: Programmers improved from 64% to 81% accuracy over 3 sets of 10 items when provided feedback on estimation errors
feedbackImprovement.source: Study: 'How Much Does Feedback and Performance Review Improve Software Development Effort Estimation? An Empirical Study', cited by Mike Cohn / Mountain Goat Software (https://mountaingoatsoftware.com/blog/are-we-really-bad-at-estimating)

estimatorTypeDistribution.description: When not told what type of estimate to provide, 37% gave optimistic, 27% most-likely, 22% did not know what type they provided
estimatorTypeDistribution.source: Magne Jorgensen research, cited by Mike Cohn (https://mountaingoatsoftware.com/blog/the-five-possible-estimates-and-which-one-your-team-should-use)

mlBasedEstimation.description: Machine learning approaches to story point estimation

dataset.name: Choetkiertikul et al. (2019) / TAWOS dataset
dataset.repositories: Apache, Appcelerator, DuraSpace, Atlassian, Moodle, Lsstcorp, Mulesoft, Spring, Talendforge

mlBasedEstimation.replicationFinding: Deep-SE does NOT statistically significantly outperform Median baseline in most cases, confounding earlier claims
mlBasedEstimation.replicationSource: Sarro et al. (2022) 'Agile Effort Estimation: Have We Solved the Problem Yet?' IEEE TSE (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.05401v2.pdf)

challenged.description: Completed but over-budget, over-time, fewer features

historicalContext.stagnation: Success rates have hovered around 30% for over a decade, showing 'stubborn persistence in failure rates' despite widespread Agile adoption

costOverruns_historical.caveat: Jenkins (2006) in ScienceDirect argued this 189% figure may be biased upward due to sampling methodology: 'a continued use of that figure as a reference point for estimation accuracy may lead to poor decision making' (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0950584905001023)

agileVsWaterfall.finding: Standish Group reports Agile projects succeed at approximately 3x the rate of Waterfall projects
agileVsWaterfall.source: Standish Group CHAOS Report 2020, summarized by The Story (https://thestory.is/en/journal/chaos-report/)

onTimeDelivery.description: 31% of IT projects are delivered on-time, on-budget with all features (all methodologies combined)

onBudgetDelivery.description: Average effort overrun is ~100% for underestimated projects (actual = 2x estimate)

averageScheduleOverrun.description: Historical range of schedule overruns for challenged projects. Standish reports 222% average; ISBSG reports late projects average ~100% overrun.
averageScheduleOverrun.source: Standish Group CHAOS Report 1994; ISBSG Estimates report

publicDatasets.description: Publicly available datasets with sprint/agile estimation data suitable for model calibration

tawosDataset.name: TAWOS (Towards Agile Warehouse of Open Source) / Choetkiertikul dataset
tawosDataset.contains: User stories/issues with ground truth story points from JIRA

jiraSprintVelocityDataset.name: Agile Scrum Sprint Velocity DataSet (RandulaKoralage)
jiraSprintVelocityDataset.contains: Sprint data for 4 open source projects: Spring XD, Mesos, Aurora, UserGrid
jiraSprintVelocityDataset.format: CSV files with issues, summaries, and sprint data

jiraEstimationPrediction.name: JIRA Estimation Prediction (jai2shukla)
jiraEstimationPrediction.contains: Agile sprint datasets and story point estimation datasets used in IEEE TSE publications

publicJiraDataset.name: Public Jira Dataset (Montgomery et al. 2022)
publicJiraDataset.description: Jira data from multiple organizations across several decades. Used in stability analysis of 926 projects from 12 organizations with over 1.6 million data points.
publicJiraDataset.source: Referenced in InfoQ article on agile predictability (https://infoq.com/articles/improve-predictability-measure-stability)

stateOfAgileReportHighlights.description: Key statistics from the annual State of Agile reports by Digital.ai (formerly VersionOne/CollabNet)
stateOfAgileReportHighlights.historicalRespondents: 40,000 total participants across all 18 years of the survey

recommendedCalibrationDefaults.description: Suggested default values for Epoch sprint_forecast tool calibration, based on aggregated public data

velocity.p85_description: Use P85 (85th percentile) velocity for sprint commitments to achieve ~85% success rate, rather than average which yields 50% failure rate

estimation.storyPointDrift_magnitude: 15-25% at 8 points, increasing for larger estimates
